ordered_diagnoses: Chronic kidney disease-mineral and bone disorder

facts.raw_span: 87-year-old Cantonese-speaking man
Alzheimer’s dementia, hypertension, stroke, hyperlipidaemia, gout, peptic ulcer, and chronic kidney disease
one week of increasing left leg pain and weakness
impaired mobility
a single episode of urinary incontinence
anorexia and a 12% body-weight loss over six months
blood pressure was 88/45 mmHg
heart rate 96/min
elevated inflammatory markers (CRP 76 mg/L, WCC 11.9 × 10^9/L, neutrophils 8.5 × 10^9/L)
pre-renal acute-on-chronic kidney injury
bilateral iliacus and iliopsoas muscle oedema with enhancement and a left-sided insertional tendinopathy
no evidence of trochanteric bursitis

concepts.why: Elevated inflammatory markers and bilateral iliacus and iliopsoas muscle oedema with enhancement are consistent with an iliopsoas abscess.
Elevated inflammatory markers and bilateral iliacus and iliopsoas muscle oedema with enhancement are consistent with pyomyositis.
Increasing left leg pain and weakness, along with elevated inflammatory markers, are consistent with septic arthritis of the hip.
History of gout and increasing left leg pain and weakness are consistent with gouty arthritis.
Increasing left leg pain and weakness, along with anorexia and weight loss, are consistent with rheumatoid arthritis.
Increasing left leg pain and weakness, along with anorexia and weight loss, are consistent with polymyalgia rheumatica.
Low blood pressure and bilateral iliacus and iliopsoas muscle oedema with enhancement are consistent with hypotension-induced muscle injury.
History of atorvastatin use and bilateral iliacus and iliopsoas muscle oedema with enhancement are consistent with statins-induced myopathy.

concepts.preferred_label: Chronic kidney disease-mineral and bone disorder
concepts.why: History of chronic kidney disease and pre-renal acute-on-chronic kidney injury are consistent with CKD-MBD.
Low blood pressure and elevated inflammatory markers are consistent with sepsis.
It explains the uncovered finding of low blood pressure at 88/45 mmHg.
It explains the uncovered finding of no evidence of trochanteric bursitis and is consistent with the insertional tendinopathy found on MRI.

rationales.F01: Age is not specific to any condition
rationales.F02: Multiple comorbidities increase the likelihood of various conditions
rationales.F03: Left leg pain and weakness could be indicative of several conditions
rationales.F07: Hypotension could be related to hypotensive shock or muscle injury
rationales.F09: Elevated inflammatory markers suggest an infectious or inflammatory process
rationales.F10: Pre-renal acute-on-chronic kidney injury is consistent with chronic kidney disease
rationales.F11: Bilateral iliacus and iliopsoas muscle oedema with enhancement is highly suggestive of iliopsoas abscess or pyomyositis
rationales.F12: Absence of trochanteric bursitis makes it less likely

frontier_selector.rationale: Elevated inflammatory markers and bilateral iliacus and iliopsoas muscle oedema with enhancement support Pyomyositis, which is a more specific diagnosis than Iliopsoas abscess given the provided evidence.
